definitions.explanation: Someone who secretly passes information to the opposing side while remaining part of their own group. Strongly negative — the word implies betrayal, not whistleblowing.

examples.japanese: {組織|そしき}に{内通者|ないつうしゃ}がいた。
examples.english: There was a mole inside the organization.

examples.japanese: {内通者|ないつうしゃ}を{探|さが}し{出|だ}すのに{時間|じかん}がかかった。
examples.english: It took time to track down the inside collaborator.

examples.japanese: {作戦|さくせん}が{事前|じぜん}に{漏|も}れていたことから、{内通者|ないつうしゃ}の{存在|そんざい}が{疑|うたが}われた。
examples.english: Because the plan had leaked in advance, the presence of a mole was suspected.

notes:
Formed from {内通|ないつう} (secret communication with the enemy) plus 〜{者|しゃ} (person who). Most at home in war stories, crime fiction, and corporate-espionage reporting.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {内通者|ないつうしゃ}を{疑|うたが}う: to suspect someone of being a mole
- {内通者|ないつうしゃ}{狩|が}り: a hunt for the informant
- {敵|てき}の{内通者|ないつうしゃ}: the enemy's inside man

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {密告者|みっこくしゃ}: informer — reports others to the authorities; not necessarily an insider serving a rival
- {裏切|うらぎ}り{者|もの}: traitor — the everyday word, broader and not limited to passing information
- スパイ: spy — planted from outside, whereas an {内通者|ないつうしゃ} is a genuine member who turns
